transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, my wife actually made the appointment. What brings me in is... I guess this memorial for my brother. It’s just gotten a whole lot bigger than I originally meant it to. I’ve been spending most of my days lately chasing down specific songs, calling folks up, planning out these big displays and trips. 

I was actually trying to track down this one specific song on an original 45 record. Jimmy really loved vinyl. We used to have this huge stereo cabinet when we were kids, heavy oak. Or maybe it was mahogany. You really don't see furniture made like that anymore, do you? Everything now is that cheap particle board. We bought a bookshelf from one of those big box stores a few years back and it took me three days to put it together, missing a wooden dowel and everything. Just terrible quality. 

But anyway, my wife, she’s upset because she says I’ve pushed aside the garden, my morning walking group, and just about everything else to work on this memorial. The walking group hasn't even been the same since Frank moved to Florida, to be honest. The humidity down there is just terrible for your joints, I don't know why everyone insists on retiring there...
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, irritable, or energized lately, even if it felt good at the time?

Energized... yeah, I suppose that's the word. I’ve just been feeling completely lit up lately. Full of purpose, you know? Like this memorial is going to be the thing that finally makes the whole town understand our family. My dad actually helped build the old community center back in '68, you know. Poured the concrete foundation himself. He always said concrete work is all about the mix. If you get the water ratio wrong, it cracks right through the first freeze. And the winters here used to be a lot worse than they are now, let me tell you. We'd get snow all the way up to the windowsills in January, you couldn't even get your car out of the driveway for days... 

But anyway, my wife says I'm irritable. And I guess I do snap at her. One minute I'm feeling great about the plans, and the next I'll just bite her head off. Or I'll snap at the folks down at the senior center if they slow me down or start questioning the display. Like Brenda down there, she had the nerve to ask why I needed three whole tables for the photos. Brenda's always sticking her nose where it doesn't belong, she's the one who ruined the Thursday morning bingo by complaining about the prize money...
Have you been sleeping less than usual lately, or feeling like you don’t really need much sleep to get by?

Sleep? Well, I don't know, I guess I haven't really been paying much attention to the clock. I've just been up working on the memorial, going through all these old boxes of photos. You wouldn't believe how many pictures my mother kept. She had this old Polaroid camera, the kind where the picture slides right out the front and you have to shake it. Though I read somewhere later that you're not actually supposed to shake them, it ruins the chemicals or something. But everybody did it back then. Just like everybody used to smoke in restaurants, right at the table while you were eating your eggs. Can you imagine that now? The waitress would just come by and empty your ashtray right next to your toast. 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, sleep. I don't really know. I just lay down when I can't keep my eyes open anymore, but there's just so much to get done for Jimmy. I don't really feel tired, though. Not like I used to. Used to be I'd need a nap every afternoon right after The Price is Right. Bob Barker, now there was a television host. That new guy just doesn't have the same charm, if you ask me.
Have you found yourself needing to keep moving, doing things more quickly than usual, or feeling restless lately?

Restless? Yeah, I suppose you could say that. I just can't seem to sit in my chair like I used to. I'm up all the time, hauling boxes down from the attic, making calls, rearranging papers on the dining room table, just pacing from room to room. It's like my body has more steam in it than a man my age ought to have. Speaking of steam, did you know the old locomotive that used to run through here back in the 50s was powered by coal? My granddad used to work down at the railyard. He'd come home smelling like sulfur and axle grease. My grandmother would make him strip down on the back porch before he could even set foot in the kitchen. She was a stickler for clean floors, always on her hands and knees with a bucket of hot water and pine soap. You don't smell pine soap much anymore. Now everything smells like artificial lemon or lavender. I bought a bottle of dish soap the other day and it smelled like a perfume counter at Macy's. I couldn't even eat my dinner off those plates, felt like I was tasting flowers...
Have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual, or that you feel rested even if you haven’t slept much?

Sleep? Didn't we just... well, I guess I already said I haven't been paying much mind to the clock. But no, I don't feel like I need less of it, exactly. I'm just busy. There's just so much to do. And you know, speaking of clocks, I found this beautiful old grandfather clock in the attic when I was looking for Jimmy's baseball trophies. It belonged to my wife's great-uncle Arthur. He was a clockmaker over in the next county. Fascinating trade, really. They don't make things with gears and springs like that anymore. Everything's digital now. Just a little battery and a screen. No soul in it. Arthur used to say a clock was like a heartbeat for a house. You know, tick-tock, tick-tock. Steady. Reliable. Not like cars these days. I took my sedan in for an oil change last week and the mechanic hooked it up to a computer! A computer! To tell him what's wrong with the engine! I told him, in my day, a mechanic listened to the engine. You could hear a loose belt or a misfiring spark plug just by the sound of it. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, sleep. Yeah, I don't know. I'm not really tracking it.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual, or that you feel rested even if you haven’t slept much?

Doc, I feel like a broken record here, didn't you just ask me that? Like I was saying, I really couldn't tell you how many hours I'm getting. I'm just not tired. I don't keep a log of it or anything. 

Speaking of logs, my wife used to keep these little spiral notebooks for absolutely everything. Grocery lists, phone numbers, recipes she saw on the morning news. You remember when they used to have those cooking segments on the Today Show? Back when Willard Scott was doing the weather. He always did those birthdays for people turning 100, putting their faces right there on the Smucker's jelly jars. Smucker's... now, my favorite was always the strawberry preserves. Not the jelly, mind you, the preserves with the actual chunks of fruit in it. You buy jelly today and it's just high fructose corn syrup and red dye. I read an article in a magazine at the dentist's office that said all that artificial dye makes kids bounce off the walls. No wonder kids these days can't sit still in school. They don't even teach cursive anymore, either. 

But anyway, what was it? Sleep. Yeah, I just lay down when I need to, I guess. I just feel fine without it right now.
Have you actually felt like you needed less sleep than usual, rather than just being too busy or distracted to sleep?

Well, I suppose I don't really feel like I need it. It's not that I'm trying to stay awake, I just... I don't have that heavy feeling behind the eyes, you know? Like when you've been driving all night. 

I used to drive a truck back in the late seventies. Hauling freight all the way from Chicago down to Dallas. Now that was a job that'd make you tired. You'd be staring at those white lines on the highway for so long they'd start to look like they were dancing. I had this old CB radio in the cab, used to talk to all the other drivers just to stay awake. My handle was "Silver Fox." Everybody had a handle back then. It was a whole community out there on the road. We'd warn each other about speed traps—"smokies," we called 'em. You don't see state troopers wearing those big hats much anymore, do you? Now they just sit in those unmarked SUVs with the tinted windows. Sneaky, if you ask me. I always thought if you're going to enforce the law, you ought to be proud to show your face. Just like a man ought to look you in the eye when he shakes your hand. A firm handshake tells you everything you need to know about a fella. 

But, uh, no, I just don't feel the need for sleep right now. I feel perfectly fine without it.
